'''Mary R. M. Bishai''' (born 1970) is an [[List of Egyptian Americans|Egyptian-American]] physicist who is a Distinguished Scientist at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. In 2023, she was elected co-spokesperson of [[Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment]], and was made responsible for the 1,400 person collaboration. She was named a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2014.

== Early life and education ==
Bishai was born to a family of engineers. Her father had a PhD in electrical engineering and her grandfather was a science teacher.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Women @ Energy: Mary Bishai |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=25272 |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=bnl.gov|publisher=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref> She grew up in [[Nigeria]] and [[Egypt]] and is of Egyptian descent.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mary Bishai |url=https://www.dunescience.org/facesofdune/mary-bishai/ |access-date=2023-03-22 |language=en-US|website=Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment}}</ref> In 1985, she read a ''[[National Geographic]]'' magazine about particle physics experiments taking place at [[CERN]], and decided that was what she wanted to work on.<ref name=":0" /> She was an undergraduate student in physics at [[University of Colorado Boulder]], then moved to [[Purdue University]] for graduate studies,<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|first=Mary R. M.|last=Bishai|year=1999|title=A study of semileptonic and 2-body decays of charm strange baryons, a search for CP violation in Xi hyperon decays and a study of surface-treated planar microstrip gas chambers|degree=PhD|publisher=Purdue University|id={{ProQuest|304523942}}|oclc=1194793889|url=https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/dissertations/AAI9951916/|website=purdue.edu}}</ref> where she worked on the [[CLEO (particle detector)|CLEO]] experiment at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=":0" /> She worked on parity violations in the decays of charm-strange baryons.<ref name=":0" /> She was awarded the Purdue University George W. Tautfest Award, an award that honors outstanding physics graduate students.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards to the Graduate Students: Department of Physics and Astronomy: Purdue University |url=https://www.physics.purdue.edu/about/prizes_awards/all_grad.html |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=Purdue University |language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 1998, Bishai joined [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] as a research associate, where she was involved with [[Tevatron]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Mary Bishai |url=https://www.bnl.gov/staff/mbishai |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref> She worked on [[quantum chromodynamics]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Nanotechnology Now - Press Release: Four Scientists With Major Contributions to Research at Brookhaven Lab Named American Physical Society Fellows |url=http://www.nanotech-now.com/news.cgi?story_id=51107 |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=nanotech-now.com |language=en}}</ref>

Bishai joined [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in 2004. She was hired to work on the [[MINOS]] experiment, a long baseline neutrino project.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Brookhaven Lab Physicist Mary Bishai Elected DUNE Co-Spokesperson |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=121011 |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref> Her recommendations enabled the CD-0 decision from the [[United States Department of Energy]] (DOE) that enabled the [[Long Baseline Neutrino Experiment]].{{citation needed|date=April 2023}} She was part of the team who measured the [[J/psi meson]] cross sections at the [[Collider Detector at Fermilab]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Acosta |first1=D. |last2=Collaboration |first2=C. D. F. |date=2005-02-03 |title=Measurement of the J/Psi Meson and b-Hadron Production Cross Sections in ppbar Collisions at sqrt s = 1960 GeV |journal=Physical Review D |volume=71 |issue=3 |article-number=032001 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.71.032001 |arxiv=hep-ex/0412071 |s2cid=35434349 |issn=1550-7998}}</ref> Her role as Project Scientist for the LBNE from 2012 to 2015 contributed to the formation of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) in 2015.<ref name=":1" /> 

Dr. Bishai also contributes as a mentor, committed to guiding young scientists in the field. This includes mentoring over 15 undergraduate students through the DOE-funded Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internship program and 5 high school student interns through the High School Research Program, both hosted by [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (BNL).<ref name=":1" /><ref name="m480">{{cite web | title=Mary Bishai Named Distinguished Scientist Fellow | website=Brookhaven National Laboratory | date=2024-08-12 | url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=121934 | access-date=2026-03-16}}</ref> Additionally, she has mentored students who visited Brookhaven as part of the African School of Physics program.<ref name=":1" />

===Awards and honors===
In 2014, Bishai was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] "for her contributions to flavour physics."<ref name=":2" /><ref name="d355">{{cite web | title=Mary Bishai to Deliver Distinguished Scientist Fellow Lecture, 1/14 | website=Brookhaven National Laboratory | date=2025-01-07 | url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=222155 | access-date=2026-03-16}}</ref>

Bishai served as the co-spokesperson of [[Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment]] (DUNE) from January 2023 through March of 2025. As co-spokesperson, Bishai was responsible for leading the 1,400 member neutrino collaboration.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brookhaven Lab Physicist Mary Bishai Elected DUNE Co-Spokesperson |url=https://www.newswise.com/doescience/brookhaven-lab-physicist-mary-bishai-elected-dune-co-spokesperson |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=newswise.com |language=en}}</ref> DUNE will send the most intense neutrino beam in the world from [[Fermilab]] to the [[Sanford Underground Research Facility]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=BNL {{!}} Staff {{!}} Mary Bishai, Physics Department |url=https://www.bnl.gov/staff/mbishai |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=www.bnl.gov |language=en}}</ref>
